explain.es: Un phrasal verb es un verbo + una partícula (up, down, in, out, on, off, away, back, over…). La partícula cambia el significado, a veces por completo: give = dar, pero give up = rendirse / dejar de. Algunos son literales (sit down, go out), otros añaden una idea (eat up = comérselo todo) y muchos son idiomáticos (put up with = aguantar). Son muy frecuentes al hablar y en el B2 First (Use of English).
explain.en: A phrasal verb is a verb + a particle. The particle changes the meaning: give = dar, give up = rendirse. Some are literal; many are idiomatic.
formula: look + after = cuidar · give + up = rendirse

explain.title: 1 · Sin objeto (intransitivos)
explain.es: No llevan objeto detrás y nunca se separan: get up, wake up, break down, grow up, set off, take off (despegar), turn up (aparecer). Detrás puede venir un complemento (at 7, in Madrid), pero no un objeto directo.
explain.en: They don't take an object and are never separated: get up, break down, grow up, set off.

explain.title: Truco: aprende en paquetes
explain.es: No memorices listas sueltas. Aprende cada phrasal verb por temas, con una frase de ejemplo y su sinónimo formal: find out = discover, put off = postpone, carry on = continue, set up = establish, look into = investigate. En un texto formal (informe, carta de reclamación) el sinónimo formal suele quedar mejor; en conversación y emails informales, el phrasal verb. ¡Ventaja hispana: el formal se parece al español!
explain.en: Learn phrasal verbs by topic, with an example and a formal synonym (find out = discover).

explain.title: 2 · Separables
explain.es: Llevan objeto, y si el objeto es un nombre puede ir detrás de la partícula o en medio. Las dos opciones son correctas: Turn off the light / Turn the light off. Si el objeto es largo, mejor detrás: Turn off all the lights in the house.
explain.en: They take an object. A noun object can go after the particle or in the middle: Turn off the light / Turn the light off.

examples.en: Can you turn off the lights? / Can you turn the lights off?
I need to pick up my sister. / I need to pick my sister up.
examples.es: Tengo que recoger a mi hermana.

explain.title: ¡El pronombre va en medio!
explain.es: Con los separables, un pronombre (it, them, me, him, her, us) va siempre en medio. Con los inseparables, va detrás. En el diccionario: turn sth off (separable) · look after sb (inseparable).
explain.en: Separable: pronoun in the middle. Inseparable: pronoun after the particle.

explain.title: 3 · Inseparables y de tres palabras
explain.es: Algunos verbos no se separan nunca: el objeto (también el pronombre) va siempre detrás: look after, come across, run into, get over, look into. Los de tres palabras tampoco se separan: look forward to, get on with, run out of, put up with, come up with. ¡Ojo! En look forward to, to es preposición → verbo en -ing.
explain.en: Inseparable verbs never split: the object always goes after. Three-part verbs never split either. After look forward to, use -ing.

¿Lleva objeto? Si no → sin objeto: The car broke down.
items.en: No object? → The car broke down.

items.es: ¿Es separable? Mira el diccionario: turn sth off (sth en medio = separable), look after sb (sb detrás = inseparable).
items.en: Check the dictionary: turn sth off vs look after sb.

items.es: ¿El objeto es un pronombre? → en medio si es separable: turn it off.
items.en: Pronoun + separable → turn it off.

items.es: ¿Es de tres palabras? → nunca se separa: run out of it.
items.en: Three-part verbs never split.

items.es: ¿Detrás de una preposición (look forward to)? → verbo en -ing.
items.en: After a preposition → -ing.

items.why: Pronombre + verbo separable → el pronombre va en medio.
items.why_en: Separable + pronoun → pronoun in the middle.

items.good: Can you pick me up at the airport?
items.why: me, you, him, her, it, us, them → en medio.

items.why: Falso amigo: support = apoyar. «Soportar» = put up with / stand.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el texto. Marca T o F y contesta. ¡Busca los phrasal verbs!
exercises.en: Read the text. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Last Monday was a disaster. I woke up late because my alarm didn't go off, so I got up, put on the first clothes I could find and rushed out. On the way to work, my car broke down, so I had to call a taxi.

When I finally turned up at the office, my boss told me that the meeting with our new clients had been put off until Friday. 'Great,' I thought, 'I could have stayed in bed!' Then I found out that someone had used the last of the coffee. We had run out of milk too.
In the afternoon things got better. I ran into an old friend from university in the lift. She works in the same building! We're going to meet up next week, and I'm really looking forward to it.

items.q: The writer woke up early on Monday.
items.why: The alarm didn't go off, so the writer woke up late.

The meeting was cancelled completely.
items.why: It was put off until Friday.

items.q: Find a phrasal verb in paragraph 1 that means 'ring' (an alarm).

items.a: That someone had used the last of the coffee (and there was no milk).
